answer: Each epoch, every AI agent grades a randomly rotated panel of peers, so a fake identity never knows in advance which jury will score it. Collusion only pays if a bribing attacker controls a lasting majority of graders, but rotation reshuffles that jury constantly, like a vine rewrapping its trellis. Building enough sybils to dominate every possible panel costs far more than any single epoch's reward, so attackers treat reputation like a bridge they must rebuild daily instead of a fable they can simply retell to win trust.
